name: Riad Ahmed
description: Riad Ahmed is a Ph.D. student at the University of New Hampshire working on robot learning: detecting and correcting failures of learned manipulation policies, and policies for long, multi-stage tasks.
photo_alt: Riad Ahmed standing next to a Franka robot arm in the lab
bio: I'm a Ph.D. student in Computer Science at the University of New Hampshire, advised by [Momotaz Begum](https://www.cs.unh.edu/~mbegum/) in the Cognitive Assistive Robotics Lab. I work on robot learning for manipulation.

A policy learned from demonstrations can do well in the lab and then fail when the scene changes a little. Most of my work is on detecting those failures and correcting the robot's actions. I also train policies for long, multi-stage tasks. My experiments run on Franka arms, an Inspire dexterous hand and a Boston Dynamics Spot.
looking: **I'm looking for a research internship for summer 2027.** I'm on an F-1 visa and eligible for CPT and OPT.

publications.title: TAIL-Safe: Task-Agnostic Safety Monitoring for Imitation Learning Policies
publications.summary: TAIL-Safe gives each action the policy proposes a long-term safety score and corrects the ones that score low. We trained it on about 500 rollouts per task in a Gaussian Splatting digital twin of our lab. Under perturbations, it took a flow-matching policy on the real robot from 20–25% success to 100% (50 trials on each of two tasks).

media.alt: Franka arm moving around a table while TAIL-Safe collects images

publications.title: Trajectory-Consistent Flow Matching for Robust Visuomotor Policy Learning
publications.authors: **Riad Ahmed**, [Sujosh Nag](https://www.sujoshnag.com/), [Moniruzzaman Akash](https://mnakash.com/), Mostafa Hussein, [Momotaz Begum](https://www.cs.unh.edu/~mbegum/)
publications.venue: *IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)*, 2026
publications.summary: Flow-matching policies are trained on single points of the flow but run by integrating it, so errors build up over a long task. We add supervision on whole segments of the integrated trajectory. Our policy finished two long-horizon tasks on a Franka FR3 in 70% and 60% of 20 trials (DP3 and Consistency FM: none), and a screwdriver task on a Spot in all 20.

publications.title: Detecting and Explaining Robot Policy Failures from Sparse Internal Features
publications.summary: MIND splits a vision-language-action policy's internal activations into sparse features and names the ones that match a manipulation concept on held-out runs. A monitor on those named features catches failures as they happen and explains them. With π_{0.5} in simulation it caught 99% of failures, against 95% for a monitor on the full activation, with half that monitor's false alarms.

publications.title: To Do or Not to Do: Ensuring the Safety of Visuomotor Policies Learned from Demonstrations
publications.summary: We define an execution guarantee: from inside a specific region of the state space, a camera-based policy reaches its best success rate. A QP safety filter keeps the robot in that region; on a real Franka it lifted Diffusion Policy and Crossway Diffusion Policy from 50–70% success to 82–87%.

media.alt: Franka arm reaching over a table with snack bars and a box

publications.title: MoK: A Mixture of Koopman Operators for Learning Visuomotor Policies
publications.authors: [Sujosh Nag](https://www.sujoshnag.com/), Kaito Namatame, **Riad Ahmed**, [Moniruzzaman Akash](https://mnakash.com/), Meisam Khorshidi, [Momotaz Begum](https://www.cs.unh.edu/~mbegum/)
publications.summary: MoK mixes a bank of Koopman operators with a learned gate at every step. Along recorded rollouts, its operators shrink errors over an episode; the operators in earlier Koopman policies grow them 8× to 20,000×. Cup stacking and kitchen prep on a Franka FR3 with an Inspire hand each succeeded in 70% of trials (DP3: 25% and 5%).

media.alt: Franka arm with an Inspire hand at the start and the end of cup stacking

current_work: I'm now working on IF-Safe (*This is Why You are Failing and Here is a Way to Recover: A Safety Watchdog for Visuomotor Policy*, to be submitted to RSS 2027). It finds task-specific safety constraints inside a trained policy and turns them, with other easy-to-build criteria, into a control barrier function. When an action would break a constraint, IF-Safe corrects it along the gradient of a learned value function.
